events.text: I woke up this morning... and every single guy on Earth was gone.
No dads. No brothers. No annoying guys in my group chat.
Just me.
Okay. Not gone. Asleep.
Because in this world... guys hibernate.
On the first snow of the year, every boy and every man falls asleep like a bear, and doesn't wake up until spring.
You see, every November, dads start eating like it's their full time job.
My dad calls it bulking for winter.
My mom calls it the annual fridge crisis.
He even has a secret snack stash, with a lock, and a sign that says...
Don't touch. I'll know.
Every school turns its gym into a giant hibernation hall.
Three hundred guys in sleeping bags, snoring in perfect harmony.
And my grandpa snores so loud, the news reports it as an earthquake.
Me? I have never hibernated. Not once in fifteen years.
The doctor says my sleep gene is broken. Like a loading bar that's stuck at ninety nine percent.
So every winter, I'm the only guy awake in the whole town.
Kids call me The Night Shift.
Usually, my mom lets me stay home all winter. Just me, my games, and a lot of silence.
But this year, I turned fifteen. And my mom had other plans.
Then last Monday, the first snowflake fell.
Brayden was in the middle of his favorite thing. Talking about Brayden.
This year, I'm finally asking Lily to the Winter Dance, because let's be honest, I'm basically the most...
Face first. Into the snow. Mid sentence.
My dad fell asleep with a slice of pizza still in his mouth.
Coach fell asleep mid whistle. The whistle kept going for three hours.
In five minutes, every guy in town was out cold.
Except me.
You know what this means.
I get to play video games for four months straight?
It means you're going to school.
So on Tuesday, I walked into Maple High as the only guy in the entire building.
Six hundred girls. One me.
Nobody said a word. For like... ten whole seconds.
And then everyone had questions.
Why aren't you asleep? Are you a vampire? Can you open this jar?
Turns out, when you're the only guy, everyone thinks you're an expert in guy stuff.
Attempt one. The jar.
I pulled so hard I saw my ancestors. The jar did not move.
She opened it with one hand. While texting.
Attempt two. The spider.
I screamed louder than the entire class combined.
Attempt three. Fix the projector.
I pressed one button. The fire alarm went off. I still don't know how.
My big sister found me in the hallway.
You are embarrassing the entire male species.
Technically... I am the entire male species right now.
Then, at lunch, the principal made an announcement.
The Winter Dance will still happen, on the last night of winter. Everyone, bring a partner.
Six hundred heads turned. Slowly. Toward me.
There was exactly one partner available in the whole school. And it was me.
By the end of lunch, there was a sign up sheet on my locker.
Two hundred names by fourth period. Five hundred by sixth.
By the end of the day, even my sister had signed it. Just so she could cross her name out.
But honestly, there was only one name I cared about.
Lily. She sits in the back of art class, and draws in a little blue sketchbook.
She was the only person who never asked me for anything.
And every morning, there was a hot chocolate waiting on my locker. No name. Just a tiny drawing of a snowflake.
I had no idea who it was from.
Subscribe, because this is where things get really weird.
Because that night, I got hungry. At three in the morning.
And my dad's secret snack stash was open.
Half of it was gone. And the sign still said...
I'll know.
But my dad was in his room. Asleep. Snoring.
Which meant only one thing. Someone else in this house was awake.
So I set traps.
Night one. Flour on the floor. In the morning, there were footprints. Fuzzy slipper footprints.
Night two. A bell on the cupboard. It didn't ring. Someone had stuffed a sock in it.
Night three. I hid in the pantry. And I waited.
At three in the morning, the fridge light came on.
Someone in a bathrobe was eating my dad's cookies.
It was... Grandpa.
Evening, kiddo. Want a cookie?
You're awake?
Every winter. For sixty years.
But the earthquake snoring?
Bluetooth speaker.
The broken sleep gene runs in the family. It skips a generation.
Then why do you pretend to be asleep?
Because when you're the only guy awake, everybody wants something from you. You've noticed, huh?
Fifty years ago, I stopped pretending for one winter. For one girl.
He showed me an old photo. Him and Grandma, at the Winter Dance. The only couple on the dance floor.
Six hundred people want a dance partner, kiddo. Only one of them wants you.
That's when I realized something.
Nobody needed me. They needed a partner. Any partner.
And three hundred partners were already in the gym. Asleep.
So I went to the principal with a plan.
Start the dance at eleven thirty. On the last night of winter. In the gym. Right next to the hibernation hall.
And why would I do that?
Because the forecast says the snow melts at midnight.
The night of the dance, the gym looked amazing. Lights, music, and three hundred snoring guys along the wall.
And six hundred girls in one very long line. All waiting for me.
Eleven fifty eight. I could see Lily in the back. Alone. Drawing.
I walked past the whole line.
Sorry. I'm taken. Well, I'm hoping.
Eleven fifty nine.
Midnight.
The snow melted. Spring came. And three hundred guys sat up at the exact same time.
...handsome guy in this whole entire school!
He finished his sentence. Four months later. In his pajamas.
Suddenly, everyone had a partner. And the dance went absolutely crazy.
But I was at the back of the gym.
Was it you? The hot chocolate?
Lily didn't say anything. She just opened her sketchbook.
It was full of tiny snowflakes. And drawings of me. Losing to a jar.
You looked lonely. Being the only one awake.
Everyone wanted the only guy. I just wanted you to have a hot chocolate.
So I asked her the only question that mattered.
Do you want to dance?
I thought you'd never ask.
And for the first time ever, I was glad I was awake.
The next morning, my dad woke up and walked straight to his snack stash.
It was empty. And the sign still said...
I'll know.
He looked at me. I looked at Grandpa.
Grandpa was snoring. Very loudly. With a speaker in his pocket.
Fifty years. And Grandpa has never once been caught.
Subscribe if you would stay awake for someone. And comment what you would do if you were the only guy awake.
